title: The work list
dek: What is being done here, as opposed to what is known.
lead: Every other register in this archive answers what is **known** — [what has been searched](/searched/), [what is still open](/open-questions/), [what was got wrong](/corrections/). None of them answered **what is being done**, so that lived in a chat window, which is the one place that does not survive the session. Three times in one week someone asked this archive what it was working on, and three times the answer was typed out and then lost. This is that answer, written down. It is deliberately short on findings and long on **who has to move each thing** — an item with no owner is how a list becomes wallpaper.
close:
Written 15 September 2026, in the shape the Defranceschi session settled on, so that eight archives keep one list rather than eight people each inventing one.

**Extended the same day into a roadmap.** The first twenty-two rows were what happened to be in hand. Rows 23 to 48 were built instead from what the archive already knows about itself: `coverage.json` says **34 of the 70 direct ancestors have no document**; `targets.json` ranks every filmed book by how many of them it would reach; `consistency.json` and `impossible.json` hold **116 contradictions** the tree has never been asked to explain. The rows are in yield order, and the yield is measured rather than guessed — **Karlobag deaths reach ten direct ancestors and that book's A–Z index is already mapped to the letter**, which is why it is row 23 and not row 40.

Three of them are not research at all but the conditions for it: **twenty-one ancestors have no place recorded**, so no film can be chosen for them (row 34); **a DGS number does not reliably name a book** (row 42); and **nobody has written down which parish the record index covers**, so every sitting rediscovers whether its next job is an hour or a week (row 43).

rows.what: Rebuild the Žubrinić households of Šumećica by house number — all fifteen read
rows.note:
**All fifteen read, 15 September 2026, and [question 4](/open-questions/) 4d is answered: the Michaels are at least seven men, in seven houses, in four villages.** **Šumećica N° 5** (four children, 1849–58), **Šumećica N° 10**, **Poljica N° 13**, **Prozor N° 50**, **Obilje N° 7** and **Prozor Br. 1** — six distinct wives. The *Conditio* column separates them and nothing else does.

**Šumećica N° 5 is a household this archive did not have** — Michael Žubrinić and Maria Marković, four children across nine years. The Šumećica houses known before were N° 2, N° 10 and N° 24.

**Three Žubrinić women married Žubrinić men**, and the index carries a given name only for every one of them. **The index is also wrong at least once**: it gives the 1852 mother at Šumećica N° 5 as «Maria Maković» where the register says **Marković** — a household that looked like two is one.

The last entry, Maria of 28 November 1858, came in a third window: **Prozor N° 49**, next door to N° 50. Everything is in `sources/familysearch/otocac-michael-1846-1858.json`, and the cautions that cost this sitting time are in `notes/otocac-michael-house-numbers-2026-09-15.md` — the book **changes language from page to page**, the **status word drifts while the house number holds**, and entries hide in the last row of a left page below where a whole-page crop stops.

**Reconciled against the tree.** The households are not new people: all six wives and nine of the fourteen children are already there. **What the tree lacked was the house numbers** — of those nine children exactly one carried one, *Nikola Miko Žubrinić*, «Prozor 50», which this reading confirms; the rest said «Otočac, Croatia» or nothing. Seven are now in `sources/readings.psv`, and **five children genuinely absent from the tree** are in `sources/found.psv`, every one of them with siblings the tree already has.

**A caution worth more than the finding.** A first check concluded that none of the six wives was in the tree. That was wrong: they appear only as **parent references on their children**, with no page of their own, so a search of published people misses them. **Searching `people.json` is not searching the tree**, and a «not in the tree» claim made that way is worthless.

rows.what: Karlobag folios 6 and 4 — and ahnentafel 54's marriage, found on folio 4
rows.note:
**Found 15 September 2026, where this row expected a null.** Ahnentafel 54 married ahnentafel 55 at Karlobag on **17 June 1807**, folio 4, image 231: «…habito mutuo consensu ***Georgii filij defti Georgii Uroda*** et ***Mariæ filiæ Michaelis Gergas*** hujatium… præsentibus testibus *Caspare Jerko viduo* et *Joanne Fero…*». The date column reads 17 and the month is a ditto for the entry above it, *16 Junii*; the page runs 7 Jan · 14, 22, 26 *ejusdem* · 3 Feb · 7 May · 16 Jun · **17** · 8 Jul · 20 Sep, so the ditto can only be June.

**It proves the two brothers.** The 1806 marriage of *Joannis filii defuncti Dñi Georgij Uroda* was read at the time as probably a brother rather than ahnentafel 54 himself, because ahnentafel 55's 1834 death entry calls her husband a *Georgius*. Confirmed from the other side: **Joannes and Georgius are both sons of the same dead Georgius Uroda**, married sixteen months apart in the same church. Ahnentafel 108 is named here as «defti Georgii Uroda», tying the 1791 burial to both marriages.

**Two cautions.** The volume's own index put a Georgius Uroda on **folio 6** — folio 6 has now been read **end to end, both pages, 1809 and 1810 through to the «Finis», and holds no Uroda at all**. The index's *folium* column does not reliably name the leaf. And the doubt carried as «Martini U[roda?]» in the 18 January 1809 entry reads, at five times full resolution, **Uzelac** — settled, and not a lead. Full record in `notes/karlobag-1807-uroda-gergas.md`.

rows.what: Selce deaths — ahnentafel 25 read, three ancestors still to find
rows.note:
**Ahnentafel 25 is read, 15 September 2026.** LIBER DEFUNCTORUM p. 144, image 397: «**Udova Maria Antić, supruga pok. Josipa, kći Jurja i Mare Jeličić, R. Katolikinja**» — Selce house **29**, aged **73**, died **6 July 1882**, buried the 7th. Widow of ahnentafel 24, daughter of ahnentafel 50, and the age matches a birth of 22 March 1809. The mother is written «Mare» where the tree has ahnentafel 51 as *Margarita* — consistent, not proof, recorded as read.

**The index does not cover this register, which changes how the rest gets done.** A sweep for *Antić* at Selce returns **119 indexed entries and every one is a baptism**. The index-with-ARK shortcut that found the Otočac households and the Karlobag baptism in minutes **does not work here** — this book has to be walked.

**So the film is mapped instead.** 005497948 is 802 images and is not one book: image 200 is a *HISTORIA PAROCHIAE*, the death register runs through the 380s–390s, image 600 is a later Croatian-ruled register, and **the waypoint in the URL changes between images**. Measured: **384 = 1877**, **397 = 1882**, **400 = 1883–84** — about **2.7 images to the year**.

**Still wanted:** ahnentafel 24 (21 Oct 1850, interpolates to ≈ image 311), and ahnentafel 48 and 49 (both 1829, ≈ image 254). Both 1829 estimates sit well outside the measured range and the film changes books more than once, so check the page heading before reading. Arks in `sources/familysearch/film-005497948-selce-deaths.json`.

rows.what: Senj marriages 1734–1858 — the marriage of ahnentafel 12 and 13
rows.note:
Their son was baptised **1 November 1857**, so the marriage falls just before it. Their register names are now known exactly — **«Juraj Papa, težak»** and **«Matia rođena Pilipić»** — which is what makes this findable. Not in the index; a film read.

**The FamilySearch block of 15 September 2026 comes and goes — see [row 21](/worklist/).** It shut three times and opened three times in forty minutes, and fifteen register entries were read in those windows. This row is not blocked; it is waiting for the next window, with its targets written down.

rows.what: Ahnentafel 53's baptism — found: Oliva Maria Smojver, 11 March 1781
rows.note:
**Found 15 September 2026.** «Ego Joës Antonius Frankovich Parochus Loci baptizavi Infantem ***die 11ma*** hujus natam ex ***Vincentio, et Oliva Smoyver, vulgò Vukić***, Conjugibus hujus Civitatis, cui imposui est nomen ***Oliva Maria***» — Karlobag, page 65, ark `3:1:3QS7-L99C-L998-5`. The month column reads *Ejusdem* under *Martij*, and the next opening begins at 19 March, so **11 March 1781**. The tree had only «MAR 1781».

**It confirms ahnentafel 106 and 107 from the register side** — Vicentius Smojver Vukić and Oliva Bacchi were in the tree but had never been put on a page; one line now names the couple and the child together.

**And it gives a by-name in a parish that had none.** «Smoyver, ***vulgò*** Vukić» — this archive's by-name file was built out of Selce, where the connectors are *aliter · dictus · dicti* and the scribe **underlines** the pair. Karlobag uses ***vulgò*** and does **not** underline. It also explains a name the tree carries without comment: ahnentafel 106 is recorded as «Vicentius Fabiano Smojver **Vukić**» as though Vukić were part of the surname. It is the household name, and the clerk said so.

**A film note this corrects.** `holdings.psv` gives DGS 5481648 as the 1691–1804 baptisms and `notes/karlobag-films.md` calls it a **327-image** film with «image 220 = Anno Domini 1782». Film 005481648 actually has **596 images** and its image 216 is headed **«Godine 1845»**. The 1771–1804 baptisms are under a different waypoint, and the way in was the **record index**, not the film number. Full record in `notes/karlobag-1781-oliva-smojver.md`.

rows.note:
**Bribir** 1678 onward — its own parish, filed here as a village of Grižane until the catalogue was read properly. **Sv. Juraj kod Senja** 1697–1852, not in the parish table at all. The **Karlobag *Stanje duša*** beyond the U section. The **Grižane *Popis duša* of 1738**, a household census a century older than Otočac's. All four are in [holdings.psv](/searched/) with their film numbers.

rows.note:
Image 75. Every other *Pagus* in the book was mapped — Ottosaz, Luka, Dubrava, Novoselia, Lieška, Kostelievo Selo, Obilje, Beljue, Šumećica — and this one resisted. Small, but the map is otherwise complete and a hole in it will be noticed.

rows.what: Reconcile the stale «pending» rows in the searched register
rows.note:
**Done 15 September 2026.** Three rows were retired, not edited: **Ancestry**, **FamilySearch — Rijeka registers** and **FamilySearch — Otočac, Stanje duša** were *placeholders* — «never», «not yet», «still unread» — and each had been superseded by a real row recording the actual reading. The register was **over-reporting what is outstanding**: eleven pending, of which three were already done. Seven now, and every one of them genuinely open.

**The gate that stops it recurring.** Every register row now declares a `key` — the body of material it covers — and `tools/searched.py` **refuses** when a row is *pending* while any other row with the same key carries a real outcome. The key is there because the source *name* cannot do this job: «Senj marriages, 1734–1858» is genuinely unopened while «Senj marriages, 1859–1920» is read end to end, and a gate matching on names would have called the first one stale and sent a sitting to re-read a book that was already finished. A gate that cries wolf is worse than no gate.

The same stale claim had spread into prose: `/searched` still named **four portals «never once searched»** when all four had been opened, and `requests/README.md` and `REPLIES.md` still said the three letters were **not yet sent** when they went on the 15th. All corrected.

rows.what: Decide where ahnentafel 108 and 109 live
rows.note: **Georgius Uroda** and his wife **Maria** were read out of a register this week and are real. The tree stops at ahnentafel 54 and this archive does not edit the tree — that separation is what the whole project rests on. They are recorded in `sources/found.psv` with ten others, but **nothing on the site shows them** yet. Whether a found person should appear beside the tree, and how, is a decision about what this archive *is*, not a task.

rows.what: Waiting on the Državni arhiv u Rijeci
rows.note: Sent 15 September to **obrada@riarhiv.hr**. It asks for one identified volume: the Rijeka baptismal register covering **1 March 1892**, which the film skips — the volumes run 1886–90, 1890–91, then **1900–01**, and the alphabetical *Kazalo* skips the same span. **This is the only route left to [question 13](/open-questions/)**, and to Juraj's marriage with it.

rows.what: Waiting on the Župni ured Senj
rows.note: Sent 15 September to the parish priest. Three deaths after the film stops in 1907 — including **Milka Papić**, whose 1886 baptismal entry carries a registrar's 1971 annotation citing **page 280, line 37** — the January and February 1895 baptisms, and whether a *stanje duša* survives for Senj.

rows.what: Waiting on Župa Krmpote, via Ledenice
rows.note: Sent 15 September. Asks for **Juraj Blažević's baptism**, most likely 1855–70 and before the film begins — the single entry that would name his father and settle the join five generations rest on. **One question in that letter has since been answered here**: Tonka's date is **25/27 October 1884**, read off the register, and the reply should be read against that rather than the other way round.

rows.note: Sent 13 September, **acknowledged and queued on the 14th**, nothing since. Gospić holds Otočac and Karlobag — which is to say the Žubrinići and the Urode.

rows.what: Arolsen Archives — needs a browser this machine cannot provide
rows.note: `collections.arolsen-archives.org` refuses this machine. It is the likeliest route to anything on **Senj, 1943**, and it has never been searched. Ten minutes in an ordinary browser.

rows.what: The alphabet nodes are probably not only a Žubrinić problem
rows.note: Fifteen nodes named with a single capital letter — **«M Žubrinić Xubrinich Zubrinic»** — were being published as parents of 75 real people and as one another's siblings. A card index typed in as a family. Both the bucket detector and the site's junk filter now refuse them, **but all seven archives share one GEDCOM**, and nothing here has checked whether the same drawers exist under Blažević, Papić, Prpić or Kalanj. **The test is four lines** and belongs in the kit rather than in this archive.

rows.what: Five methods found here that the other archives will need
rows.note:
**The index gives the image.** FamilySearch's record search returns the **image ARK** of every indexed entry, so a record opens at the page in one step instead of being hunted down a film — that single fact produced most of this week's findings. **A third FamilySearch failure state**: a sign-out takes *everything* (503, redirect to the sign-in host) where a rate-limit blip and a session block leave the catalogue answering — written into `tools/familysearch.md`. **And `sources/found.psv`**, somewhere to put people read out of a register whom the tree does not have; every archive here will hit that wall.

**Fourth — the register cannot be trusted to retire its own rows.** `/searched` here said eleven sources were outstanding when three had been read and closed: each was a «not yet» placeholder left standing because the reading went into a *new* row. Over-reporting what is outstanding is the same lie as under-reporting it, and it costs a sitting that re-opens a finished book. The fix generalises: **every row declares a `key` naming the body of material it covers, and the checker refuses a *pending* row when another row with that key has a real outcome.** The key is the whole trick — matching on the source *name* would flag «Senj marriages, 1734–1858», which is genuinely unopened, against «Senj marriages, 1859–1920», which is read end to end. Every archive that keeps a search register has this bug waiting in it. In `tools/searched.py` here.

**Fifth — there is a fourth FamilySearch failure state, and it is the worst one.** Beside the rate-limit blip, the session block and the sign-out, there is **Error 15**: a 403 «Access Denied» interstitial on *every* path, laid on the egress address rather than the session. Signing in again does nothing. **The diagnostic that tells it apart in one call** is to fetch a Deep Zoom `image.xml` for an ark that read successfully before: a blip or a session block leaves the tile edge answering, and Error 15 takes the tiles down too. If the tiles are gone there is no route to a page and the only moves are to wait or to read from a different network.

rows.what: Another session's kit upgrade is sitting half-landed in this working tree
rows.note:
**The styles.css instance cleared** — whoever wrote the burger-menu fix has committed or discarded it, and it is gone from the tree. A second instance took its place the same day.

`site/package.json` and `site/package-lock.json` now pin the kit at **`f55559d`** where the last commit here pinned **`60aad58`**, and `node_modules/` holds the newer one. Nothing in this archive's build script installs anything, so the bump was made by **the kit session running `npm install` in this shared tree**. It is real work — `f55559d` gives `WorkList.astro` the ring that links each archive's work list to the others — and the kit has already moved **one commit past it** (`27cfb83`), so the bump is mid-flight rather than finished.

**Landed by its own session, 15 September 2026** — commit `eb41806` pins the kit at `d1e902e`, past both the version that appeared in this tree and the one after it, and the working tree is clean again. Leaving it alone was the right call: the session that owned the upgrade finished it two commits further on than the state found here.

**Left uncommitted deliberately at the time.** This archive's build passes against the newer kit (check:kit, check:living and check:worklist all green), so nothing is broken; but committing another session's half-landed upgrade would take the decision of *which* kit commit the estate stands on away from the session making it. Every `git add` here stays scoped to `sources/ tools/ site/src/ notes/ requests/`.

rows.what: Read the Otočac status animarum to find the Žubrinići
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake and kept here rather than deleted.** Two sittings went into this book on the assumption it held the family. It does not: Šumećica occupies images 102–106, and every household in them is **Dašović, Štabinčić, Orehović, Janežić, Ollar, Kovačić or Orehovački** — no Žubrinić, no Domus 2, no Domus 24. The book gave the village map and a clean negative, and it will not give the house. **The baptism registers replaced it** — that is row 1.

rows.what: Find Juraj Blažević's baptism in the Krmpote film
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake.** The plan named this «the reachable target» on the strength of a catalogued range of *1815–1896*. The film begins in **1879** and Juraj was born in the 1860s; Krmpote is one film, one item, and there is no other Krmpote book. Ledenice and Novi Vinodolski were checked the same way and hold no candidate. **What survives is the letter** — row 12.

rows.what: Harvest house numbers from the Otočac baptisms of 1834–46
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake, and it was this archive's own.** The morning's plan said *every* entry writes the household into the *Conditio* column. **That book does not**: its *Conditio* holds one status word — *Confiniarius*, *Decurio* — checked at December 1839 and March 1845, with the place column giving only «Ottoccii». Ahnentafel 10's January 1834 entry is an early-book habit the parish dropped. **House numbers are readable for 1846–58 and for the first years of 1834, and not in between.**

rows.what: FamilySearch blocks this browser intermittently — work in the windows, not around them
rows.note:
**Error 15, and it comes and goes.** On 15 September 2026 every request to `familysearch.org` began returning **403 «Access Denied — Error 15»** as a full interstitial. It shut at 04:21, opened at 04:30, shut at 04:45, opened at 04:47, shut at 04:51 and opened again at 05:00. **Fifteen register entries were read in those windows**, which is the whole of work list row 1.

**So the lesson is not «wait for it to clear».** It is to have the targets — ARKs, dates, parents — written to disk *before* a window opens, so a ten-minute opening is ten minutes of reading rather than ten minutes of searching. That is what `sources/familysearch/otocac-michael-1846-1858.json` is, and it is why row 1 closed on a day when the site was mostly shut.

**The one-call diagnostic.** Fetch a Deep Zoom `image.xml` for an ARK that read successfully before: a rate-limit blip or a session block leaves the tile edge answering, and Error 15 takes the tiles down too. If `image.xml` returns HTML instead of `<?xml`, there is no route to a page — not the index, not the catalogue, not the scans. Signing in again does nothing; the block is on the egress address, not the session.

**Client IP 168.140.255.212.** Reading from David's own browser on his own network would not be behind this address at all.

rows.what: The people found beside the tree are recorded but never published
rows.note:
`sources/found.psv` holds **seventeen people read out of a register whom the tree does not have**, two of them on the direct line, and `tools/found.py` builds `site/src/data/found.json` on every regeneration. **No page imports it.** The data is generated, gated and invisible.

Found while adding five Otočac children to it and trying to link `/searched` at the page that shows them — the register gate refused the link because there is no such page, which is the gate doing exactly what it is for.

This matters more than a missing page usually would: the whole argument for `found.psv` is that a person read out of a register should stand **beside** the tree rather than be pushed into it. A file nobody can read does not stand anywhere. It wants the same treatment as `/corrections` and `/open-questions` — one page, grouped by family, each row carrying its citation.

rows.what: Karlobag deaths 1774–1804, led by the book's own A–Z index
rows.note:
**Corrected 15 September 2026 before it was begun: this is a walk, not a lookup.** The row was written asserting the Karlobag deaths could be reached through the FamilySearch index. They cannot — row 43 tested four surnames and **every Karlobag hit is a baptism**; the 1717–1861 range that suggested otherwise is baptisms throughout.

**The highest-yield target in the archive, and it is already mapped.** `targets.json` says the Karlobag death books reach **ten direct ancestors** — ahnentafel 52, 55, 104, 105, 107, 108, 110, 111, 212 and 220 — more than any other book here. Four of them have **exact death dates inside the 1774–1804 volume**: ahn 212 Josiph Smojver Vukić **16 May 1776**, ahn 104 Jacob Pilipić **10 April 1778**, ahn 220 Nicolaus Gerkacs **30 October 1783**, ahn 105 Catherina Luckinić **29 May 1790**. Ahn 108's burial of 10 September 1791 is already read out of this same book.

**And it needs no walking.** `holdings.psv` records the register at images **356–409** and its **KAZALO A–Z at 410–434, with the letter positions measured** — P.R at 428, R.S 429, S.T 430, T.U 431, U.V 432, V.X 433. Look up *Pilipić*, *Smojver*, *Gerkacs* and *Luckinić* in the index, take the folium, convert with the known folio map (left pages EVEN, folio 62 = image 388), and read four ancestors in an afternoon.

**What the index page actually looks like, now it has been opened.** Image 428 is **P on the left page and R on the right** — the big letter is written at the top centre of each *page*, three column-groups to a page, each *Cognomen · Nomen · dies · folium*. **The entries are ordered by folio, not alphabetically within the letter**: folios 104, 104, 105, 105, 105, 106, 106, reading Perpich · Perpich · Perpich · Perpich · Potocgniak · **Pekkas** · Potocgniak. So a surname is found by scanning the letter's pages, not by jumping to it. Folio converts to image as **image = 388 + (folio − 62) ÷ 2**, left pages even.

**A find already, from the one index page opened:** *«Pekkas Magdalena, 5 Augusti, folio 106»*. **Pekass is three of the direct ancestors with no document** — ahn 213, 426 and 427 — and this is the first time the surname has appeared in a register here at all.

rows.what: Karlobag deaths 1804–1861 — the later half of the same ten
rows.note: The other half of row 23's ten. Ahnentafel **52** (Josephus Pilipić, d. 26 June 1828), **55** (Maria Gerkacs, d. 6 August 1834 — the entry already quoted here as «uxor piscatoris Georgii Uroda», but never read out in full), and **111** (Lucia Tomljanović, d. 19 September 1809) all fall in the 1804–1861 volume, which has **its own index** on the same film. Do it after row 23, with the index technique already proved.

rows.what: Selce deaths — the six direct ancestors still unread
rows.note:
Row 3 read ahnentafel 25 and mapped the film. **Six remain in the same book**: ahn **24** (Josephum Antić, 21 Oct 1850), **48** (Joannis Antić, 13 Mar 1829), **49** (Margarita Lončarić, 15 Jul 1829), **96** (Joannis Antić, 27 Feb 1793), **98** (Pauli Lončarić, 29 Sep 1811) and **99** (Anna Papić, 24 Aug 1807). `targets.json` scores this book **19 reachable of 19** — the only book in the archive where every reachable person is a direct ancestor or their sibling.

**The catch is that Selce is not indexed for deaths** (row 43), so this is a walk. The measured points are in `sources/familysearch/film-005497948-selce-deaths.json`: 384 = 1877, 397 = 1882, 400 = 1883–84, about 2.7 images to the year. The 1790s and 1800s entries sit far outside that range and the film changes books more than once.

rows.what: Karlobag baptisms — the seven direct ancestors still unread
rows.note: The Karlobag birth books reach **nine** direct ancestors (13, 26, 27, 52, 53, 54, 55, 105, 106); ahnentafel 53 was read on 15 September. **Seven left**, and three of them — 54 (b. 22 Apr 1777), 105 (b. 30 Mar 1727) and 106 (b. 18 Jan 1754) — have exact birth dates to aim at. The 1771–1804 volume's arks and the route into it are in `sources/familysearch/film-karlobag-baptisms-1771-1804.json`; **note that its film number is not the one `holdings.psv` gives** (row 42).

rows.what: Otočac baptisms 1834–1858 — ninety-one reachable, and two ancestors
rows.note: `targets.json` scores this book **135 people, 91 reachable**, second only to Novi Vinodolski, and it carries ahnentafel **10** and **21**. It is also the book whose *Conditio* column produced the seven Šumećica and Prozor households in row 1 — so every entry read here pays twice, once for the person and once for the house number. The index covers it (that is how row 1 was done), so this is index-led, not a walk.

rows.what: Otočac deaths — ahnentafel 40 at Šumećica N° 2, and ahnentafel 20
rows.note: **Ahnentafel 40, Toma Žubrinić, died 4 January 1838 and the tree places him at «Šumećica 2»** — the same house the 1856 and 1858 baptisms of row 1 put Nicolaus Žubrinić in. A death entry naming the house would **tie the direct line to a house number that is currently only inferred**, which is the whole of question 4. Otočac deaths run 1780–1836 and 1834–1858, so January 1838 is in the second book. `targets.json` also puts ahnentafel **20** in these books.

rows.what: Senj baptisms 1734–1894 — seventy-three reachable, and ahnentafel 3 and 6
rows.note: **94 people, 73 reachable**, carrying ahnentafel **3** and **6** — the closest generations to Seka herself that are still unread. The Senj marriage books have been verified end to end, so the parish is known ground; the baptisms have only been sampled. Note the hard edge: **Senj births stop at 1894**, which is what makes questions 1e and 5b unreachable (row 33 of the register's «unreachable» list) and why the Senj parish letter was written.

rows.what: Senj deaths — ahnentafel 27 read, two ancestors still to find
rows.note:
**Ahnentafel 27 is read, 15 September 2026.** Senj death register, ark `3:1:3QS7-899X-1HVP`, entry 13 of 1886: «**1886 dne 9 veljača · Matija PILIPIĆ, žena · Vicko PILIPIĆ, fin. stražar u miru, njezin muž · Karlobag · rim. kat. · 78 · Marasmus senilis · Providjena**».

Three things are new. **Ahnentafel 26 gets an occupation** — *fin. stražar u miru*, a **retired finance guard**; nothing here had said what he did. **Her origin is recorded as Karlobag**, independently confirming the birthplace of the daughter whose 23 April 1810 birth fixed her parents' marriage — found the same day as **17 June 1807**. And the register's **age of 78** against a computed 75 is recorded as written, not as a correction: the age is what the informant said, the birth has a baptism behind it.

**She was missed at first because she is indexed under Pilipić, her married name** — a search for *Uroda* returns nothing at Senj.

**Still to find: ahnentafel 26** (Vicko Pilipić, d. 14 November 1897) and **ahnentafel 8** (Toma Blažević, d. 26 July 1907). Ahn 8's burial is already located — indexed at **28 August 1907**, ark `3:1:3QS7-899X-14XR` — and **the month between the tree's death date and the register's burial date is itself worth reading**. Ahn 6 (d. 1939), ahn 7 (d. 1935) and ahn 3 (d. 1971) all fall after the book closes in 1907 and are unreachable on film.

rows.what: Krivi Put baptisms 1847–1884 — fifty-eight reachable, and ahnentafel 7
rows.note: **100 people, 58 reachable**, carrying ahnentafel **7**. Only one Krivi Put page has ever been opened here (the 1859 baptisms, recorded *partial*). The catalogue range was verified on 14 September, so the book is known to cover the window.

rows.what: Novi Vinodolski 1650–1900 — the largest reach in the archive, and no ancestor in it
rows.note: **132 people, 120 reachable — the highest count of any book here — and not one direct ancestor.** That combination is exactly why it keeps being deferred, and exactly why it should be done deliberately rather than by accident: it is **breadth, not depth**, and it would settle a great many collateral lines at once. It is also the **earliest register in the estate** — the 1650 book was opened once and its earliest leaves are in **Croatian, not Latin**, which is a finding in its own right. Do it when the direct line is exhausted, or when a wet afternoon wants volume.

rows.what: Krmpote-Vodice and Ledenice births — the Blažević side
rows.note: The two Blažević ancestors without a document, **ahn 16 (Anton) and ahn 32 (Ilija, b. 1790)**, are both placed at **Smokvica Krmpotska**. Krmpote-Vodice births score 15 reachable and Ledenice 15 more. **The trap is recorded and must be respected**: Krmpote's catalogue label says 1815 and **the film actually begins in 1879** — verified by opening it — so Ilija of 1790 is *not* in it. Ledenice (1734–1894) is the book that could hold him, and Krmpote is administered from Ledenice to this day.

rows.what: Twenty-one direct ancestors have no place at all
rows.note:
Of the **34 direct ancestors without a document**, **21 have no place recorded — not a village, not a parish, in several cases not a date either**: ahn 22, 41, 64, 80, 84, 85, 86, 87, 97, 100, 101, 102, 103, 109, 128, 210, 211, 213, 427, 428, 429. **No amount of film-reading reaches them**, because nothing says which film to open. This row is the precondition for half the rows above it.

The method that works is the one that found ahnentafel 55's father: **a person with no record of their own is named in their child's**. Every one of these twenty-one has a child in the tree; the child's baptism or marriage entry names the parent and usually the village. So the job is to **work down from the children**, not up from the parents.

rows.what: Gologorica is «unknown» in the parish table, and twenty-three people sit behind it
rows.note: `parishes.psv` carries **Gologorica** with *unknown* in all three range columns and the note «Istria — likely a different collection entirely». `targets.json` puts **23 people** behind it. It is the only parish in the table that has never been resolved at all. One catalogue search decides whether it is reachable or whether it joins the unreachable list honestly.

rows.what: Twenty-five children born after a parent had died
rows.note: `consistency.json` holds **71 contradictions** and the largest class is **child-after-parent-death, 25 of them**. Each is either a wrong date, a wrong link, or two people merged into one — and this archive has already found all three kinds. They are cheap to triage against the register readings now on disk, and every one resolved either corrects the tree or produces a `corrections` row.

rows.what: Twenty-four parents who were too young
rows.note: The second and fourth classes in `consistency.json`: **parent-too-young (16)** and **parent-under-seventeen (8)**. In a district where the register routinely records a bride's age, these are testable rather than arguable — and the commonest cause in this tree so far has been **a grandparent and a parent sharing a name**, which is precisely the trap row 1 documented for the Otočac Michaels.

rows.what: Ten children born before their parent was born
rows.note: `consistency.json`'s **child-before-parent-birth, 10 rows** — plus the singletons **died-before-born**, **impossible-generation-gap** and **married-before-birth**. These cannot be softened by interpretation the way an age gap can; each is a definite error in the data and should be resolved or struck.

rows.what: Forty-five impossible rows, twenty-seven of them at the record level
rows.note: `impossible.json` carries **45 rows** in four causes: **record 27**, **generation 9**, **hedged 5**, **namesake 4**. The *namesake* four are the same class of problem as the seven Michael Žubrinići, and the method that separated them — **the house number in the Conditio column** — now exists. Worth re-running the four against what row 1 established before treating them as insoluble.

rows.what: Fifty-one duplicate groups, twenty-three of them live
rows.note: `duplicates.json`: **51 groups**, of which **23 are live** and 28 already rejected. A live duplicate group is two tree records that may be one person — which is the same question as the two Georgius Urode and the seven Michaels, and it now has a settled method. **28 have already been rejected**, so the remaining 23 are the hard ones and deserve the register rather than judgement.

rows.what: Re-sweep for by-names now the connector list is wider
rows.note: The by-name file was built out of **Selce and its neighbours**, where the connectors are *aliter · dictus · dicti* and the scribe **underlines** the pair. Karlobag, found on 15 September, uses ***vulgò*** and does **not** underline. So the sweep that produced 17 phrases **was looking for the wrong shape in every parish except one**. Re-run it across the pages already read with the connector list widened — *vulgò · alias · rečeni · zvani* — and against the surnames the tree carries as double-barrelled, which is where a by-name hides once it has been absorbed (ahnentafel 106 «Smojver Vukić» was exactly that).

rows.what: Audit the film numbers in holdings.psv against the actual films
rows.note:
**A film number in this archive does not reliably name a book.** `holdings.psv` gives DGS **5481648** as the Karlobag 1691–1804 baptisms; opened by that number it has **596 images** and image 216 is headed **«Godine 1845»**. The 1771–1804 baptisms are under a different waypoint entirely. `notes/karlobag-films.md` describes the same film as **327 images**. Film 005497948 turned out to be **802 images and at least three books, with the waypoint changing between images**.

So: **walk every DGS number in `holdings.psv`, open it, record its image count and what its first, middle and last openings actually are, and store an ARK for each landmark** — because an ARK resolves to exactly one image and a DGS number demonstrably does not resolve to exactly one book.

rows.what: Which parishes the record index covers, and for which events — answered
rows.note:
**Answered 15 September 2026, and it re-orders the rows above it.** Eight surnames of this family were swept through the index and tallied by place and event type; the result is in `sources/familysearch/index-coverage.psv`.

**Indexed for baptisms only — these are walks, not lookups:** **Otočac** (165 baptisms, not one death), **Selce** (77, confirmed twice), **Karlobag** (four surnames tested, every hit a baptism, range 1717–1861), **Krmpote-Vodice**.

**Deaths are indexed:** **Senj** — also under the Latin place string ***Senia***, which a search for «Senj» misses — **Krivi Put**, **Novi Vinodolski**, and thinly **Crikvenica**.

**This corrected row 23 before it was started.** That row was written asserting the Karlobag death index reached ten ancestors; the earlier evidence for that was a Karlobag date range of 1717–1861 which turns out to be **entirely baptisms**. Row 23 is a walk through the book's own KAZALO, not an index lookup — and the KAZALO is ordered **by folio, not alphabetically**, so a surname is found by scanning, not by jumping to a letter.

**And a trap worth more than the map.** Ahnentafel 27 is indexed under **Pilipić**, her married name — a search for *Uroda* returns nothing at Senj. **A married woman's death is indexed under her husband's surname.** Every sweep for a maiden name will walk past her.

rows.what: Twenty-five villages in the targets file are unplaced
rows.note: `targets.json` carries **25 unplacedVillages** — place strings from the tree that no parish in `parishes.psv` claims. Each one is either a spelling the gazetteer does not fold, a village in a parish not yet in the table (which is how **Bribir** and **Sv. Juraj** were added on 14 September), or a place outside this family's districts. Until they are placed, the people standing on them cannot be routed to a book.

rows.what: Re-grade the thirty-one walls after this week's reading
rows.note: `walls.json` carries **31 walls** — 9 unplaced, 7 nameless, 6 outside, 4 unchecked at the last count. **This week moved several of them**: ahnentafel 53, 54 and 55 gained documents, ahnentafel 25 gained a death, and the Karlobag and Selce film ranges are now verified rather than assumed. A wall that has quietly stopped being a wall is worse than one that never was, because it goes on deterring work.

rows.what: Fifty-six of the seventy-two graveyard memorials match nobody
rows.note:
`graves.json` holds **72 memorials from the Otočac cemetery survey** and **only 16 are matched to a person**. The other 56 are photographed, transcribed and unattached. Some will be collateral lines, some will be the *found* people of row 47, and some will be strangers — but they were photographed on the ground at cost and they are the only source here that nobody else can re-read.

The house numbers from row 1 give a new handle: a stone naming a Žubrinić of Šumećica or Prozor can now be tested against seven known households.

rows.what: Decide which of the eighteen found people are really tree people
rows.note:
`found.psv` holds **18 people read out of a register whom the tree does not have, two of them on the direct line**. But «the tree does not have them» was established by name-matching, and **this archive has already been wrong about exactly that**: on 15 September a check concluded that none of six Karlobag wives was in the tree, when all six were there as **parent references with no page of their own**. Searching `people.json` is not searching the tree.

So each of the 18 needs re-testing against parent and spouse references, not just published names — and the ones that survive are then candidates to be offered to the GEDCOM rather than kept beside it. Pairs with row 22, which publishes them.

rows.what: Two emigration threads with no route in
rows.note: Both are in the register as *pending* and neither can move without a decision that is not this archive's to make. **FindMyPast — Port Pirie electoral rolls**: eleven of nineteen read, and the trial expired before the rest; the rolls give an address and an occupation year by year, which is how a household is watched over time. **Southern Rhodesian immigration 1953–65**: an entire country known from two words on a later record, and **no route into it has been identified at all** — which is a different thing from having searched and found nothing. Both want either a subscription or a decision to let them stand as honest nulls.
